result.summary: In 2015 Zuckerberg twice put a date on AI goals: in the 30 June Facebook Q&A he said he hoped to deliver AI image understanding 'in the next 10 years', and in a Fast Company interview published 16 November he named a five-to-ten-year goal of better-than-human AI at the primary senses. reply_text:
I found two dated AI predictions Mark Zuckerberg made in 2015. I saw both only in news reports, not on a page of his own, so a checker should still go to the original source.

1. **30 June 2015, Facebook town-hall Q&A** (Computing.co.uk report). He talked about AI that can describe a photo to a blind person, then said "This is all within our reach and I hope we can deliver it in the next 10 years." The article says he wrote this in a Q&A on Facebook's own website, but I didn't open that post. Two cautions: the report may have shortened the passage, so it isn't clear exactly what "it" covers. And the line usually headlined from this session, "Our goal is to build AI systems that are better than humans at our primary senses," has no date attached in what I read.
2. **Fast Company interview, published 16 November 2015**. "One of our goals for the next five to 10 years is to basically get better than human level at all of the primary human senses: vision, hearing, language, general cognition." I opened the Fast Company article, but the paywall cut it off before this line. I read the quote in a Business Insider repost on Yahoo Finance Singapore. The exact interview date isn't given.

Ruled out or not checked:
- **3rd-quarter results call, 4 November 2015.** I read the official transcript. The only AI forward look is that the assistant M "over time will use AI to help people complete tasks," which has no date.
- **The widely quoted "five or 10-year" perception prediction** (PCWorld) is from the 27 April 2016 results call, so it's listed under other years.
- **Not checked:** the 28 October 2015 town hall at IIT Delhi and the 15 September 2015 Q&A. I didn't open the IIT Delhi report, and the Forbes article on the September Q&A loaded without its text. I didn't find any 2015 statement on when AGI would arrive.
